scenes: Start with what Silo saw itself.
An agent opens a connection.
It passes through a part of Silo that sits outside the computer.
The agent also writes a file.
The file stays inside, and Silo sees the change from outside, on the computer's disk.
Silo writes one line for each: a fact.
It is never changed.
Some things cannot be seen from outside, such as which process wrote that file.
A process is one running program.
A small part of Silo, the probe, runs inside the computer and tells Silo.
That line is a report.
The agent has full access in there, so a report is only what the inside said.
An agent program, such as Claude Code, can also give its own account of itself.
That is a report too.
Facts and reports, in the order they came, are the record.
Nothing in it is changed afterwards.
One line is never both: that the file changed is a fact, and which process changed it is a report that points to it.
An opinion is what something thinks about the record: this file is code, this agent is stuck.
It is computed from the record, and kept apart from it.
It can be wrong.
So it says whose it is, and when what gave it improves, its opinions are computed again.
The rows of the record do not change.
You can give one too.
Silo asks: is this a build?
Your answer is your opinion.
Silo keeps it as you gave it.
What gives an opinion is called a classifier: a pattern, a function, a small model, or an agent.
A classifier gives opinions.
It never acts.
What an opinion can lead to comes in the film on rules and precautions.
Something computed is as sure as its least sure ingredient.
A count of facts is as good as a fact.
Mix in a report, and the result is as told: no surer than the report.
Add a judgement, and it is an opinion.
And a report or an opinion is never stored as a fact.
All the reports together account for 48 megabytes, written by the build.
From outside, Silo saw 61 megabytes change.
Silo corrects neither.
The 13 megabytes left over are shown as unattributed, and are never spread over the rest.
And where Silo lost sight for a moment, it records a gap.
The record says what it does not know.
